title: Normalized consecutive Cech coordinates from finite-cover splittings
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,x)$ with its profinite topology and left action on finite geometric fibres [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Finite etale covers are objects of [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. For every open normal subgroup $N\triangleleft\Pi$, let $(Y_N,y_N)$ be a pointed connected finite etale cover identified on its geometric fibre with $(\Pi/N,N)$, with pointed transition $Y_M\to Y_N$ inducing $aM\mapsto aN$ for $M\subseteq N$. Work in compatible universes and small indexing systems [def-weil-size-convention].
Let $(T,(p_N),t)$ be a pointed limit of this system in schemes over $X$, with $T$ connected. Suppose for each finite etale cover $Y$ there are unique marked maps $f_s:T\to Y$ indexed by $s\in Y_x$, natural in $Y$, inducing the isomorphism $\coprod_{Y_x}T\simeq T\times_XY$. Suppose these splittings factor through every $Y_N$ acting trivially on $Y_x$, with fibre formula $aN\mapsto as$. Let $d_g$ be the resulting automorphisms determined by $p_Nd_g=f_{gN}$; assume $f_sd_g=f_{gs}$ and $d_hd_g=d_{gh}$. Write $z\cdot g=d_g(z)$.
For $q\geq0$, set $L_q=\varprojlim_N\coprod_{(\Pi/N)^q}T$ in schemes over $T$. These limits exist and admit canonical isomorphisms
$$\alpha_q:L_q\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{q+1}_{/X}$$
[def-pc-fibre-product]. On each finite quotient, change relative-to-first labels $a_1,\ldots,a_q$ to consecutive labels by $a_i=g_1\cdots g_i$, with inverse $g_1=a_1$ and $g_i=a_{i-1}^{-1}a_i$ for $i>1$. The isomorphisms use this permutation of finite summands, compatibly with quotient maps. On the constant-label section for $(g_1,\ldots,g_q)$, $\alpha_q$ has vertices
$$(z,z\cdot g_1,z\cdot(g_1g_2),\ldots,z\cdot(g_1\cdots g_q)).$$
The isomorphism $\alpha_0$ is the identity of $T$. For $q=1$ and any cover with fibre $\Pi/U$ ($U$ open), its canonical sections satisfy $\mathrm{pr}_2^*s=\mathrm{pr}_1^*(gs)$ on label $g$; at a quotient $\Pi/N$ acting trivially on that fibre this is the corresponding equality of scheme morphisms on the labelled summand, before taking the limit.
The face maps omit the first vertex by $(z,g_1,\ldots,g_q)\mapsto(z\cdot g_1,g_2,\ldots,g_q)$, omit an interior vertex by replacing $g_i,g_{i+1}$ with $g_ig_{i+1}$, and omit the last by dropping $g_q$. Degeneracies insert $1$. All these are identities of scheme morphisms between the inverse limits, verified after projection to every finite cover, and the $\alpha_q$ are compatible with them. In particular the first face need not descend to a morphism $\coprod_{(\Pi/N)^q}T\to\coprod_{(\Pi/N)^{q-1}}T$ at a fixed $N$: its new base vertex depends on the full first label. Its finite equations use that new base vertex and the quotient labels.
For a sheaf of groups $H$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and a right $H$-torsor (an $H$-sheaf locally isomorphic to $H$ with its right translation action), choose a section $e$ after pullback to $T$. Define the transition section by $e(z\cdot g)=e(z)c(z,g)$ on the double overlap, with pullbacks of coefficients understood. Then on the triple overlap
$$c(z,gh)=c(z,g)c(z\cdot g,h).$$
If $c$ depends only on the group label, this specializes to $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$.
Finally let $f:(X',x')\to(X,x)$ be pointed with the same hypotheses, let $T'$ have such normalized splittings and action, and let $F:T'\to T$ over $f$ preserve the marked sections under the finite-cover base-change fibre bijections. Under the isomorphisms $\alpha_q$ the induced map of Cech terms is $(z,g_1,\ldots,g_q)\mapsto(F(z),f_*(g_1),\ldots,f_*(g_q))$, where $f_*:\Pi'\to\Pi$ is the induced continuous homomorphism. This naturality respects identities and composition.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), applied to normalized finite splittings. Agent fibre-product limit, finite-label permutation and right-torsor calculations (old steps 11–12 and 15 of lem-sfb-pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover). Their full arguments are retained in the report.

proof.text: Write $E_N=\Pi/N$, $C_{N,q}=\coprod_{E_N^q}T$ and $P_{N,q}=T\times_X(Y_N\times_X\cdots\times_XY_N)$ with $q$ copies of $Y_N$, all viewed over their first factor $T$. For $q>0$, the assumed splitting identifies $T\times_XY_N$ with $\coprod_{E_N}T$. Apply finite-coproduct distribution over the base scheme $T$ to the $q$-fold product of this last object. Each product of $q$ identity $T$-schemes is $T$, by the fibre-product universal property. The resulting isomorphism $\beta_{N,q}:C_{N,q}\simeq P_{N,q}$ on summand $(a_1,\ldots,a_q)$ has projections $(\mathrm{id}_T,f_{a_1N},\ldots,f_{a_qN})$. For $q=0$ take $C_{N,0}=P_{N,0}=T$ and $\beta_{N,0}=\mathrm{id}$. The coproduct theorem supplies the actual disjoint clopen summands, rather than just a bijection of points.

source.place: Tags 01JB and 01JC, lemma-glue and lemma-glue-schemes, for the existing finite-coproduct distribution lemma; fibre-product universal property

proof.text: For a refinement $M\subseteq N$, naturality of the assumed marked maps gives $Y_M\to Y_N$ composed with $f_{aM}$ equal to $f_{aN}$. Therefore the quotient-labelled coproduct transition and the transition $P_{M,q}\to P_{N,q}$ have identical composites with every projection on every summand. Fibre-product uniqueness and the coproduct mapping property make the $\beta_{N,q}$ an isomorphism of inverse systems. Open normal subgroups form a nonempty cofiltered poset here: $\Pi$ is one, and $M\cap N$ refines any two. All indices are small by the stated universe convention.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: Set $W_q=T^{q+1}_{/X}$, with vertices $v_0,\ldots,v_q$. It has a cone to $P_{N,q}$ with legs $(v_0,p_Nv_1,\ldots,p_Nv_q)$. To verify that this is a limit in schemes over $T$, let $R\to T$ have a compatible cone to the $P_{N,q}$. Each of its last $q$ coordinates is a compatible family $R\to Y_N$ over $X$, hence gives a unique map $r_i:R\to T$ by the assumed limiting property of $(T,p_N)$. Together with the given $r_0:R\to T$, these maps give a unique $R\to W_q$ by iterated fibre-product uniqueness. The coordinate equations prove it is the required mediating map. For $q=0$, a cone to the constant identity $T$-scheme has its unique structure maps; the same argument gives $W_0=T$. Thus no general existence theorem for arbitrary scheme limits is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: Transport this limiting cone through the isomorphisms $\beta_{N,q}$ from steps 1–2. This constructs a limit of $C_{N,q}$ with apex $W_q$. For any chosen $L_q$ in the statement, the unique cone-preserving maps in both directions are inverse: each composite has the same cone legs as the identity and is therefore the identity by limit uniqueness. Denote the resulting relative-to-first isomorphism $\beta_q:L_q\simeq W_q$. This proves existence of $L_q$ and constructs its comparison without assuming that a pointwise parametrization is a scheme isomorphism. For $q=0$ use the canonical identification $L_0=T$, so $\beta_0=\mathrm{id}_T$.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: For each finite group $E_N$ permute the summands of $C_{N,q}$ by $(g_1,\ldots,g_q)\mapsto(a_1,\ldots,a_q)$ with $a_i=g_1\cdots g_i$. The inverse sends $(a_i)$ to $(a_1,a_1^{-1}a_2,\ldots,a_{q-1}^{-1}a_q)$: cancellation proves both composites are identities, also for $q=0$. Quotient homomorphisms preserve these products and inverses, so the permutations commute with all transitions. They induce inverse automorphisms $\lambda_q$ of $L_q$ by limit uniqueness. Put $\alpha_q=\beta_q\lambda_q$. The constant-label section $k_g:T\to L_q$ is the cone of inclusions into summands $(g_1N,\ldots,g_qN)$. For every $i,N$, $p_Nv_i\alpha_q k_g=f_{(g_1\cdots g_i)N}=p_Nd_{g_1\cdots g_i}$, hence limit uniqueness gives the displayed cumulative vertices as scheme maps $T\to T$. The empty product is $1$, and $d_1=\mathrm{id}$ follows from the assumed invertible action law.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: The following finite calculation fixes the meaning of the label formulas on arbitrary test schemes. For $Y$ with fibre $E=Y_x$ and $N$ acting trivially on $E$, denote its assumed finite factor by $f_{s,N}:Y_N\to Y$. For $aN\in E_N$, the map $f_{s,N}f_{aN}:T\to Y$ takes the marked point to $as$, by the given fibre formula. Uniqueness of marked maps makes it $f_{as}$. Consequently, on the summand $aN$ of $T\times_XY_N$, pulling the finite section for $s$ along the second coordinate equals $f_{as}$ along the first coordinate. After passing to the double-overlap limit this is $f_s v_1=f_{gs}v_0$ at label $g$, which is exactly $\mathrm{pr}_2^*s=\mathrm{pr}_1^*(gs)$ for a split finite cover. This is an equality of morphisms already on the finite summand whenever $N$ kills $E$.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: Define faces and degeneracies on $L_q$ by conjugating the vertex-deletion and vertex-repetition maps of $W_q$ by $\alpha$. Their underlying scheme morphisms exist by the fibre-product universal property. For a fixed $N$, the maps $L_q\to C_{N,q}$ decompose $L_q$ into clopen inverse images of the finite labelled summands. Thus an equality of maps into $Y_N$ can be checked on these clopen opens and then glued. On a consecutive-labelled open put $a_0=1$ and $a_i=g_1\cdots g_i$ in $E_N$. Its vertices satisfy $p_Nv_i=f_{a_iN}v_0$. Deleting an interior vertex $i$ removes $a_i$ from the cumulative list, so the two adjacent increments are replaced by $g_ig_{i+1}$. Deleting the last removes $a_q$ and drops $g_q$. Repeating a vertex repeats an $a_i$, giving the increment $a_i^{-1}a_i=1$. These are actual finite-quotient label equations on all of $L_q$, not just equations on constant-label sections.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: For the first face the new first vertex is $v_1$. On a finite-labelled open as in step 7 choose representatives $a_i\in\Pi$. The old equations give $p_Nv_1=f_{a_1N}v_0=p_Nd_{a_1}v_0$. Since $f_{bN}:T\to Y_N$ factors through $p_N$, for $bN=a_1^{-1}a_{i+1}N$ we get $f_{bN}v_1=f_{bN}d_{a_1}v_0=f_{a_1bN}v_0=p_Nv_{i+1}$. Thus the new relative labels are $a_1^{-1}a_2,\ldots,a_1^{-1}a_q$, and their consecutive increments are $g_2,\ldots,g_q$. The new base map is the second vertex of $\alpha_1$, whose restriction to $k_{g_1}$ is $d_{g_1}$ by step 5; this is the morphism denoted $z\mapsto z\cdot g_1$ with variable label. The equations are independent of the chosen representatives, since the finite factors depend only on their $N$-cosets. They glue on $L_q$ for every $N$, and limit uniqueness proves the stated first-face identity. No factorization of this new base map through $C_{N,q}$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: The resulting maps satisfy all simplicial identities: any two composites with the same ordered retained or repeated vertex list have the same composites with every vertex projection to $T$, hence are equal by the fibre-product universal property. Steps 7–8 identify these same morphisms with the claimed coordinate formulas, and their construction by conjugation proves compatibility of every $\alpha_q$ with faces and degeneracies.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: Let $P$ be the right $H$-torsor in the statement. Over the double overlap write $e_i$ for the pullback of its chosen section along vertex $i$. The right-torsor property gives a unique section $c_{ij}$ with $e_j=e_ic_{ij}$: this follows on any trivializing open from the formula $h_i^{-1}h_j$, and these unique sections glue by the sheaf axiom. On the triple overlap $e_2=e_1c_{12}=e_0(c_{01}c_{12})=e_0c_{02}$. Freeness gives $c_{02}=c_{01}c_{12}$. The three edge coordinates of steps 7–8 are $(z,g)$, $(z\cdot g,h)$ and $(z,gh)$, giving the claimed shifted cocycle with all coefficient pullbacks included. If $c$ is independent of $z$, substitution gives $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$. No commutativity of $H$ or trivial action on coefficient pullbacks is used.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: For the pointed morphism in the statement put $\rho=f_*$. Apply fundamental-group functoriality: base change identifies finite fibres equivariantly through the continuous homomorphism $\rho$. For $N\triangleleft\Pi$ open let $M=\rho^{-1}(N)$, open normal in $\Pi'$. Relabel summands by $(h_1M,\ldots,h_qM)\mapsto(\rho(h_1)N,\ldots,\rho(h_q)N)$ and use $F$ on each copy of $T'$. The resulting maps $C'_{M,q}\to C_{N,q}$ are compatible under refinement, so their composites with the projections of $L'_q$ define a cone and hence a map $L'_q\to L_q$. Refining $M$ further leaves this map unchanged. Continuity is used only to ensure $M$ is an allowed index, and no surjectivity of $\rho$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: This map agrees with the vertexwise map of Cech terms. Indeed on a summand $aM$ for the source splitting with cover $f^*Y_N$, the relative target coordinate is $\rho(a)N$: by preservation of marked sections, $f_{s,N}$ after base change followed by the source marked section has value $\rho(a)s$ in the target fibre, hence equals the marked section indexed by $\rho(a)s$. More explicitly the source finite map $f'_{s,M}$ has fibre formula $aM\mapsto a s$, and equivariance identifies this with $aM\mapsto\rho(a)s$; composing with the source splitting gives the asserted equality of scheme maps on each clopen labelled open. Thus after every target $p_N$ the $i$th vertex is $Fv'_i$. Limit uniqueness gives equality into $T$, and fibre-product uniqueness gives equality into $W_q$. Since $\rho$ preserves products, the cumulative-to-consecutive permutations commute as well, giving exactly $(F(z),\rho(g_1),\ldots,\rho(g_q))$.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); agent universal-property and finite-label calculations under the normalized splitting hypotheses of the item

proof.text: The identity pointed morphism induces the identity on finite fibres, hence on their automorphisms, so $\rho=\mathrm{id}$. For composable pointed morphisms, the base-change fibre bijections compose, $\tau^{f\circ f'}_P=\tau^f_P\circ\tau^{f'}_{f^*P}$. Both $(f\circ f')_*(g)$ and $f_*(f'_*(g))$ then satisfy the characterizing equivariance $\tau(g\cdot z)=f_*(g)\cdot\tau(z)$ of the functoriality lemma on every finite fibre, and an element of $\pi_1$ is determined by its evaluations on finite fibres, so $(f\circ f')_*=f_*f'_*$. The normalized $F$ maps respect identities and composition too: their composites with every $p_N$ are the same marked sections, and maps into $T$ are determined by these projections. Therefore the maps of $L_q$ just constructed respect identities and composition, by either their finite-summand formulas or their vertex projections.
